comments.content: A successful charset guess does not imply that the input is text. `jschardet` can return encodings such as ASCII or Windows-1252 for binary buffers, so `isBinaryFile` is now skipped for many binaries and they are decoded into garbled context. Retain an independent binary check (or equivalent binary/magic-byte validation) before accepting the detected encoding.

This can silently corrupt newly added characters that are not representable in the detected source encoding. In particular, `jschardet` identifies ordinary ASCII-only files as `ASCII`, so adding any Unicode text causes `iconv.encode(..., "ASCII")` to replace it with fallback characters. Treat ASCII as UTF-8, and for other legacy encodings verify an encode/decode round trip or fail/upgrade to UTF-8 rather than writing lossy output.

`iconv.decode` strips a BOM by default, while the later `iconv.encode` call does not add it back. Saving a BOM-bearing file therefore removes its BOM; this is especially problematic for UTF-16 files where consumers use it to determine byte order. Preserve whether the original buffer had a BOM and pass the appropriate `stripBOM`/`addBOM` options (or otherwise restore it).
